article.Citation: Johnson MW, Garcia-Romeu A, Johnson PS, Griffiths RR. An online survey of tobacco smoking cessation associated with naturalistic psychedelic use. Journal of Psychopharmacology. 2017.
article.Title: An online survey of tobacco smoking cessation associated with naturalistic psychedelic use
article.Substance: Psilocybin, LSD, DMT, Ayahuasca, Morning glory seeds, Mescaline, Peyote, San Pedro cactus
article.GenderCategory: male/female (306 male, 85.5%; 52 female, 14.5%; no non-binary/other category reported)

ae_events.Description: Acute anxiety during the reference psychedelic session, one of the two most common psychological negative effects reported.
Dysphoria during the reference psychedelic session, reported alongside anxiety as a psychological negative effect.
Physical discomfort during the reference psychedelic session (e.g. gastrointestinal distress, stomachache, headache).

article.IsObservational: Retrospective cross-sectional anonymous online survey of naturalistic (non-laboratory) psychedelic use; no randomization or researcher-administered intervention protocol -- clearly observational.
article.N: 1273 individuals completed the survey (enrolled), but 915 were excluded (163 non-serotonergic drug, 329 inconsistent responses, 423 <12 months since experience); N=358 is the final analyzed sample per Table 1/2/3 and is used here.
article.Substance: Multiple 5-HT2AR agonists were eligible/reported: Table 3 'Drug associated with smoking cessation/reduction' lists Psilocybin, LSD, DMT, Ayahuasca, and an 'Other' category (morning glory, mescaline, peyote, San Pedro) which the Methods section names individually as inclusion-eligible substances; listed all as comma-separated per the reported taxonomy.
article.ArmScope: Single-arm naturalistic survey with no comparator group; entire N=358 sample is psychedelic-exposed by inclusion criteria, so psychedelic_arm per schema guidance for single-arm designs.
article.PctBIPOC: Table 1 race breakdown (whole sample): White 307, American Indian/Alaska Native 6, Asian 6, Mixed 26, Other 13 (sums to N=358). Non-white = 6+6+26+13=51; 51/358=14.2%.
article.PctIndigenous: American Indian/Alaska Native = 6/358 = 1.7% per Table 1, reported directly as the indigenous subgroup; consistent as a subset of the 14.2% PctBIPOC figure.
article.AE_denominator: Results 'Other outcomes' section: negative-effects question answered by whole sample -- No 281 + Not sure 34 + Yes 43 = 358, matching N.
article.AnyAEReported: 43/358 (12.0%) explicitly reported negative effects; the 34 (9.5%) 'not sure' responses were not counted as confirmed AE presence.
article.NumDistinctAEs: Text names 3 distinct negative-effect types across two passages describing the same n=43 negative-effect reports: (1) acute anxiety, (2) dysphoria, (3) physical discomfort, for which the Discussion gives 'e.g. stomachache, headache' as illustrative examples of the same physical-discomfort category already named in Results ('such as gastrointestinal distress') -- treated as one type, not separate types, since no per-symptom counts are given and the Discussion explicitly frames them as examples of the Results-stated category.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: 43 participants (12.0%) reported 'Yes' to negative effects from the reference psychedelic experience (Results, 'Other outcomes' section).

ae_events.Johnson 2017_AE01: Discussion states negative effects 'were typically confined to the period of acute drug effects' -- this duration/persistence signal supports Mild (transient, resolves with session) per the rubric's default for expected acute drug effects; no intervention or FDA-seriousness signal reported, so MeetsFDASerious=N and InterventionRequired='.'; graded challenging_experience since in-session anxiety is CEQ-sense phenomenology per the rubric.
ae_events.Johnson 2017_AE02: Same duration signal ('confined to the period of acute drug effects') applies to dysphoria as to anxiety, supporting Mild with SeverityIndeterminate=N; classified as challenging_experience for the same reason as anxiety.
ae_events.Johnson 2017_AE03: Physical discomfort (GI distress/stomachache/headache) also described as confined to the acute drug-effect period, supporting Mild; classified as AE rather than challenging_experience since it is physical rather than CEQ-phenomenology in nature; no intervention/seriousness information reported.
